headline: Lost Palm Tree Rediscovered in Madagascar After 100 Years
meta_description: Scientists have found 28 individuals of Ravenea latisecta, a palm tree species unseen in Madagascar for nearly a century, offering new hope for conservation.
summary_short: A palm tree species missing from scientific records for nearly 100 years has been rediscovered in Madagascar. Researchers found 28 individuals in protected areas.
body:
After nearly a century of absence from scientific records, researchers have located 28 individuals of Ravenea latisecta, a palm tree species in Madagascar's Andasibe-Mantadia region. The discovery came during a 2024 survey led by Louis Aureglia of Aix-Marseille University, who and his team examined both wild populations and historical specimens preserved in herbariums. The breakthrough occurred when they found flowering trees—the key to confidently identifying the species, since male and female flowers grow on separate plants. With fewer than 50 mature individuals known to exist, R. latisecta is listed as critically endangered on the IUCN Red List, making this rediscovery significant for conservation efforts.

The findings reveal both mystery and opportunity. Researchers discovered most individuals clustered at four sites: Vohimana Reserve, Analamazoatra National Park, Mantadia National Park, and Vakona Forest private reserve. The species was first formally described from a specimen collected in 1927, yet remained undocumented for decades despite inhabiting one of Madagascar's best-explored botanical regions. "This is a good reminder that botanical exploration is far from complete," Aureglia noted. The researchers found no evidence that local communities harvest the palm, though the protected areas face mounting pressure from slash-and-burn agriculture and forest loss at their edges.

While the rediscovery brings hope, significant work remains. The team encountered no fruiting individuals during their surveys, meaning they have not yet been able to collect seeds for propagation or conservation cultivation in botanical gardens. More monitoring is needed to understand whether R. latisecta is naturally rare or whether external threats have reduced its population. The discovery underscores how much remains unknown about Madagascar's remarkable biodiversity, even in well-traveled regions.
quick_facts: 28 individuals of Ravenea latisecta found in 2024 survey
Last recorded in Madagascar nearly 100 years ago
Located in four protected areas in Andasibe-Mantadia region
Fewer than 50 mature individuals known to exist
All Ravenea palms found only in Madagascar and Comoros
